t: A classroom FPGA trainer packed with switches, lights, and a number display.
steps: Buy the Basys 3 from Digilent or Jameco for about 165 US dollars.
Get a micro-USB cable, as some stores leave it out of the box.
Install the free edition of AMD Vivado. Plan for a large download.
Download the Basys 3 master constraint file from the Digilent XDC repo.
Write a design that links each switch to its LED.
Build it in Vivado and program the board over USB.
Try the seven-segment counter lab next.
meta: Open Board. From $165. A few stores.
